subject: Post-demo: Model fit & evaluation next steps
summary: Post-demo recap with recommended models, preliminary benchmark results (TPS and latency percentiles), prompt set link, and next steps for a 48-hour eval with Solutions Engineering.
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acmehealth.com>, Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Model fit & evaluation next steps

Hi Sam / Jordan \u0014

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + suggested next steps based on what you shared about the triage workflow and API latency targets:

What we heard
- Primary goal: accurate triage + concise summaries for clinician review (avg output length ~120 tokens).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for interactive staff tools, target throughput ~50 qps across the fleet.
- Data sensitivity: PHI-adjacent; you prefer Dedicated or Private deployment.

Recommended initial model candidates (for evaluation)
- redwood-3.1 (fp16): strong cost/perf balance for summarization; good natively for clinical phrasing.
- llama-2-70b-q4_0 (quantized): higher throughput per GPU but watch for small regressions on clinical paraphrase/precision tasks.

Attached: preliminary benchmark csv (redwood_prelim_benchmarks_acme_20260303.csv) with single-GPU throughput and latency percentiles across your canonical prompt set. Also shared a prompt set link in the note below.

High-level perf highlights from the attached run (seq_len ~128, batch-aware):
- redwood-3.1 (fp16): p50 45ms, p95 120ms, approx 8 TPS/GPU sustained under continuous batching
- llama-2-70b-q4_0: p50 75ms, p95 240ms, higher max TPS but wider tail latency on worst-case prompts

Next steps I propose:
1) Sign off on the enclosed prompt set (attached acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl).
2) Run a 48-hour evaluation on a Dedicated node (we'll mirror your mixed load with small bursts).
3) Schedule a 60-min technical kickoff with Dylan to capture exact throughput constraints and instrumentation needs.

Can you confirm that the attached prompt set represents a fair sample? If yes, I\u0019ll have Dylan schedule the kickoff and we\u0019ll spin up the eval.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

--
Attachments: redwood_prelim_benchmarks_acme_20260303.csv, acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl

From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acmehealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model fit & evaluation next steps

Thanks Alex \u0014 very helpful recap. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we sign off on the prompt set:

1) The latency numbers look promising. Can you share TPS numbers and percentiles for a mixed workload where ~30% of requests are long (seq_len ~1024) and 70% are short (seq_len ~64)? We care about tail behavior on the long ones.
2) For the quantized variant (llama-2-70b-q4_0), can you quantify the observed regression on clinically sensitive paraphrase tasks? Any examples / delta metrics you can share would help us decide whether to accept a small quality tradeoff for cost.
3) We\u0019ll need SOC 2 + access to audit logs to move to Dedicated. Is that already part of the package for Dedicated trials?

If these answers look reasonable we\u0019ll sign off on the prompt set and move forward with the 48-hour eval.

- Sam
Director, Clinical AI | Acme Health

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acmehealth.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model fit & evaluation next steps

Hi Sam \u0014 thanks, great questions. Answers below and I included an expanded verified-profile CSV (redwood_verified_profiles_acme_20260304.csv) that breaks out mixed-workload numbers and a small qualitative regression audit on the paraphrase prompts.

1) Mixed-workload throughput / latency (attached table is per-GPU sustained under our eval harness):
- redwood-3.1 (fp16): mixed (30% long/70% short) p50 85ms, p95 230ms, sustained ~6 TPS/GPU; long-only p95 ~420ms.
- llama-2-70b-q4_0: mixed p50 120ms, p95 470ms, sustained ~10 TPS/GPU; long-only p95 ~780ms.

Notes: quantized model gives higher steady TPS but increases tail on long-sequence workloads. We instrumented KV cache reuse and continuous batching\u0014results above include those optimizations.

2) Quality regression on paraphrase/clinical-precision tasks (summary of the audit included in the CSV):
- Measured delta on relevant metrics (token-level F1 / clinically-sensitive entity preservation): redwood-3.1 baseline vs llama-2-70b-q4_0 shows avg F1 drop ~2.8 points on the curated paraphrase set. On ~200 human-annotated examples, ~6% of outputs had minor entity rewording that would require human catch.
- We\u0019ve attached anonymized examples in the CSV (rows flagged) so you can review concrete cases.

3) SOC 2 / audit logs: yes \u0014 Dedicated trial includes SOC 2 Type II evidence and requestable audit logs within the Private control plane. I\u0019ll loop in our security contact if you want a formal evidence package; Vanessa can coordinate.

Suggested path given your latency SLO and clinical precision requirements:
- Primary eval model: redwood-3.1 (fp16) for baseline quality.
- Performance-only eval: run llama-2-70b-q4_0 to validate throughput economics and measure regression impact on your critical prompts.
- If we see unacceptable regression, we can try redwood-3.1 with a more aggressive quantization profile (fp16->q4_0 tuned) or enable conservative fallback routing for critical routes.

Next actions I\u0019ll take after your sign-off:
- Dylan will schedule the technical kickoff and prep the Dedicated eval nodes.
- I\u0019ll share the Doc (https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/ACME-2026-03) and HubSpot deal link so we can track progress.

Are you available Thursday (03/05) 9-10am PT for the 60-min kickoff?

Thanks,
Alex

--
Attachments: redwood_verified_profiles_acme_20260304.csv

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model fit & evaluation next steps

Looping in a quick internal note plus public calendar invite I just sent to Sam/Jordan.

Alex \u0014 I reviewed the attached CSV and the paraphrase regression samples. Two quick operational notes:
- For the 48-hour eval, we should run redwood-3.1 with KV cache persistence enabled and a mixed-batch policy that mirrors their traffic (to avoid inflated p50 while tail spikes). I\u0019ll include the exact autoscale profile in the kickoff doc.
- On the paraphrase regression: recommend we include a small guardrail in the eval that measures entity preservation rate and a simple F1 threshold; if llama-2-70b-q4_0 falls below the threshold we\u0019ll enable model-variant routing so critical routes stay on redwood-3.1.

I added the following deliverables to the mutual action plan:
1) Eval infra provisioned (Dedicated test node) \u0014 ETA 24 hours after sign-off
2) 48-hour mixed workload run with telemetry collection (latency p50/p95/p99, TPS, cache hit rate)
3) Regression audit report (human review + metric deltas)

I\u0019ll bring the autoscale policy and the exact perf harness command to the kickoff.

\u0014Dylan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
